items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: owes its debts to Hindemith and Stravinsky and Bartok and Ravelle

ctx.x: This is a group which is made of extremely competent musicians, all of whom I know personally, and for whom I have the greatest respect as musicians, but who have literally no relation to jazz at all. There is no jazz derivation, and there is no, no, what I would call jazz intent. This kind of a group is a direct offspring of European chamber music, modern European chamber music, and owes its debts to Hindemith and Stravinsky and Bartok and Ravelle. And, uh...

Okay, but how do you fit in the fact that, for instance, they have, uh... Oh, uh... One of the players plays a bass, and there's a beat that's, uh... That's a rhythmic beat that is, uh... identified with jazz or with Afro-American...
